sentences.zh: 比如说，那些治疗受伤什叶派战士的军医有时会报告说，

sentences.en: that the Shia fighters, even gravely wounded, would try to bite them or harm them in some way, even though they were gravely wounded.
sentences.zh: 这些什叶派战士即使身受重伤，也会试图咬他们或以某种方式伤害他们，哪怕他们已经伤势垂危。

sentences.en: That was the level of commitment.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的坚定程度。

sentences.en: So we hear a lot about that the Iranian people are ready to rise up, that they're ready to overthrow this government.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经常听到传言说伊朗人民已经准备好起义，他们准备推翻这个政府。

sentences.en: But at the same time, we have seen extreme levels of commitment, even to the point of a million plus casualties.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们也看到了极端的坚定程度，甚至付出了上百万伤亡的代价。

sentences.en: How are you judging sort of the state of the Iranian opposition at this moment?
sentences.zh: 你如何评估目前伊朗反对派的状态？

sentences.en: Is it brittle?
sentences.zh: 它很脆弱吗？

sentences.en: Is it fragile?
sentences.zh: 它不堪一击吗？

sentences.en: Or are you seeing that 47 year long commitment continuing?
sentences.zh: 还是你看到那种长达47年的坚定信念仍在延续？

sentences.en: Yeah, I really want to go two lines on this.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的很想从两个方面来谈谈这个问题。

sentences.en: The first is that question.
sentences.zh: 首先是那个问题。

sentences.en: I don't know because the Iranian opposition is not really evident.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，因为伊朗反对派其实并不明显。

sentences.en: We saw in 2009, they came in the streets and they were sort of beaten back into submission and then reportedly thousands of Iranians protesting were killed by the regime in recent
sentences.zh: 我们在2009年看到他们走上街头，但随后他们被镇压回去了，据报道，最近

sentences.en: months.
sentences.zh: 几个月里，成千上万抗议的伊朗人被政权杀害。

sentences.en: But I couldn't name the opposition leader.
sentences.zh: 但我说不出反对派领袖是谁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I couldn't tell you the liberation front of Iran.
sentences.zh: 我也说不出伊朗解放阵线的名字。

sentences.en: And I know that the Shah's son is going around, but I don't think he's a legitimate alternative.
sentences.zh: 我知道那个沙阿的儿子到处活动，但我认为他并不是一个合法的替代人选。

sentences.en: I think that we can't gauge the actual strength of the desire of Iranian people to change.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们无法真正衡量伊朗人民想要改变的真实意愿的强度。

sentences.en: And of course, a war will often cause people to coalesce around their government, to coalesce around.
sentences.zh: 当然，战争往往会让人们凝聚在他们的政府周围，凝聚在。

sentences.en: In your really well-written article today, you said something I really believe in.
sentences.zh: 在你今天这篇写得极好的文章里，你讲了一件我深表赞同的事。

sentences.en: You said, I'm an American.
sentences.zh: 你说，我是一个美国人。

sentences.en: I want our side to win.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们这一方赢。

sentences.en: I feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我也有同感。

sentences.en: Even though I disagree with many of the things my government's doing, I'm unequivocal on this side.
sentences.zh: 尽管我并不同意我政府所做的很多事情，但在这一点上我是坚定不移的。

sentences.en: And that may be the case.
sentences.zh: 情况或许确实如此。

sentences.en: The other thing I want to talk about, though, is because you brought up the Maduro raid, there are three great seductions that happened to American administrations and to military.
sentences.zh: 不过，我想谈的另一件事是，既然你提到了针对马杜罗的突袭，美国政府和军方曾遭遇过三大迷思。

sentences.en: The first is the idea of covert action.
sentences.zh: 首先是秘密行动的概念。

sentences.en: And a new president comes in, and he's told by the intelligence community, we can create this great effect, and it will be covert.
sentences.zh: 新总统上台后，情报部门会告诉他，我们可以制造出这种巨大的效果，而且它是秘密进行的。

sentences.en: No one will ever know who did it, and it'll just be a good outcome.
sentences.zh: 没有人会知道是谁干的，结果自然皆大欢喜。

sentences.en: And in my experience, it never stays covert, and it rarely works.
sentences.zh: 但以我的经验，它从来都保密不了，也几乎从来没起过作用。

sentences.en: But it's seductive because it seems like an easy approach to a naughty problem.
sentences.zh: 但它之所以诱人，是因为它看起来像是解决棘手问题的一种简单途径。

sentences.en: The second seduction is, which I lived as a part of, is the surgical special operations raid.
sentences.zh: 第二种我曾亲身经历过的迷思，就是外科手术式的特种作战突袭。

sentences.en: And that is probably epitomized by the Maduro raid.
sentences.zh: 这大概以突袭马杜罗为典型代表。

sentences.en: And I would argue that we demonstrated extraordinary competence that night, but not much changed.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，那天晚上我们展现了非凡的能力，但并没有改变太多东西。

sentences.en: I don't think that we actually demonstrated the ability to change the facts on the ground to any extent, which gets to the third great seduction, and that's air power.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们实际上并没有表现出在任何程度上改变现场事实的能力，这就引出了第三大迷思，也就是空中力量。

sentences.en: And we all love air power.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都热爱空中力量。

sentences.en: In World War II, we went into the war with the Duhay theories that air power, the bomber, will always get through, and therefore air power will be dominant.
sentences.zh: 在二战中，我们带着杜黑的理论投入战争，即空中力量、轰炸机将永远突破防线，因此空中力量将占据主导地位。

sentences.en: And it was certainly very, very contributory, but it was never dominant.
sentences.zh: 它当然发挥了非常非常大的作用，但它从未占据主导地位。

sentences.en: When we got into Vietnam, which was the classic case, and we developed a strategy that said for North Vietnam, we will have a re-estat and an escalation strategy, and we will raise
sentences.zh: 当我们进入越南战争时——那是一个典型的案例，我们制定了一项针对北越的战略，即推迟和升级战略，我们要不断提高

sentences.en: the pressure on them until we hit the point at which they're willing to quit.
sentences.zh: 对他们的施压，直到达到他们愿意罢手的那个临界点。

sentences.en: It's not worth it anymore.
sentences.zh: 觉得再打下去不值得了。

sentences.en: What we didn't perceive is like the Shia wounded that your medics ran into, there was no point for North Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我们没有意识到的是，就像你那些医护兵碰到的什叶派伤员一样，对北越来说根本没有什么临界点。

sentences.en: They were asymmetrically committed to the outcome.
sentences.zh: 他们对最终结果有着不计代价的执着。

sentences.en: And so we've entered Iraq in 2003 with shock and awe, and then we spent a decade there fighting
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在2003年带着“震慑”战术进入伊拉克，然后在那里度过了十年

sentences.en: after it, I think that we fell for the seduction that if we bomb key targets, that we will produce the outcome we want.
sentences.zh: 之后，我认为我们陷入了一种迷思，即认为只要轰炸关键目标，就能达到我们想要的结果。

sentences.en: But the outcome's in the minds of the people.
sentences.zh: 但结果是存在于人们心中的。

sentences.en: And unless you're going to kill all the people, you may not affect that outcome.
sentences.zh: 除非你打算把所有人赶尽杀绝，否则你可能根本无法影响那种结果。

sentences.en: So we may be at a point, you use the word in your article, quagmire, but we may be at a point where we've run into a country that has an extraordinary capacity to be bombed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能正处于这样一个节点——你在文章中用了“泥潭”这个词——但我们可能正遇到这样一个国家，它有着惊人的承受轰炸的能力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: General, let me make the case to you that has been made to me about air power in this current war.
sentences.zh: 将军，让我向你转述一下别人向我提出的关于这场当前战争中空中力量的观点。

sentences.en: And that is, David, everything that you've walked through from the daylight bombing raids in 1943 to the air war over Kuwait, you know, during Desert Storm, all of those things, we
sentences.zh: 那就是，大卫，你从1943年的白昼轰炸到科威特上空的空战——你知道，在沙漠风暴行动期间——你所经历的一切，我们当时

sentences.en: just weren't as capable then as we are now.
sentences.zh: 就是没有现在这么强大的能力。

sentences.en: We have loitering drones.
sentences.zh: 我们有了徘徊侦察无人机。

sentences.en: We have high visibility over the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 我们对战场有着极高的可见度。

sentences.en: We have, in connection with the Israelis, we have deep penetration into the Iranian regime.
sentences.zh: 我们与以色列人合作，对伊朗政权进行了深入渗透。

sentences.en: This time it is different.
sentences.zh: 这一次不一样了。

sentences.en: This time we have more capability.
sentences.zh: 这一次我们有了更强的能力。

sentences.en: What's your response to that argument?
sentences.zh: 你对这种说法有什么回应？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Since I've retired from the military, I've been involved in some investing.
sentences.zh: 自从我从军队退役后，我一直参与一些投资工作。

sentences.en: And I love that line, this time it's different.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢那句台词：“这次不一样了”。

sentences.en: And I go, okay.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，好吧。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: The capability is so much more.
sentences.zh: 能力确实强大得多。

sentences.en: And I have to keep an open mind that it is possible that the dynamics has changed so much that we finally hit a tipping point where it will be decisive.
sentences.zh: 我必须保持开放的心态，动态可能真的发生了如此巨大的变化，以至于我们终于触及了一个决定性的引爆点。

sentences.en: But I'm not seeing that and I don't feel that.
sentences.zh: 但我没有看到这一点，也没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And the other part that I would bring out is we thought really early in Afghanistan that the people on the ground who we were targeting would be awed and intimidated by the bombing and that they would respect our capability.
sentences.zh: 我想提出的另一部分是，在阿富汗战争的早期，我们曾以为那些作为我们打击目标的当地人会被轰炸所震撼和威慑，他们会敬畏我们的能力。

sentences.en: In many ways, what we found, particularly with the tribal members, they were disdainful of it.
sentences.zh: 但在许多方面，我们发现，特别是那些部落成员，他们对此极为不屑。

sentences.en: They knew you could bomb them, but they said, if you're not willing to get down on the ground, look me in the eye and fight me mano wa mano, then you are not morally on my level.
sentences.zh: 他们知道你能轰炸他们，但他们说，如果你不敢走到地面上来，直视我的眼睛，和我一对一地战斗，那么你在道德上就不配与我平起平坐。

sentences.en: And I think that we can't forget that people fight because of their passions.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们不能忘记，人们是因为满腔热血而战。

sentences.en: It's not a geopolitical calculation that's going to drive what Iran does eventually.
sentences.zh: 最终驱使伊朗行动的不会是什么地缘政治算计。

sentences.en: It will be what's in their hearts.
sentences.zh: 那将取决于他们内心的信念。

sentences.en: And so this idea of decapitating the regime and we've got this current leader where we killed his father and we killed his wife.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种斩首政权的想法——我们现在的这个对手，我们杀了他父亲，我们杀了他妻子。

sentences.en: We apparently banged him up pretty good.
sentences.zh: 显然我们把他打得够惨。

sentences.en: And then we say, well, that will make him more willing to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 然后我们说，好吧，这会让他更愿意去谈判。

sentences.en: It wouldn't have that effect on me.
sentences.zh: 这种事发生在我身上，我可不会这么想。

sentences.en: No, and it's 100% opposite of my own experience in dealing with Al-Qaeda.
sentences.zh: 没错，这与我当年对付“基地”组织的亲身经历完全相反。

sentences.en: So, you know, one of the things that I, you just sort of see this when you've been in the military and you're out of the military.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，有些事情——当你在军队待过又退役之后，你就会有这种直观感受。

sentences.en: One thing I'm very grateful for is that the military is still the most highly respected public institution in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我非常感激的一点是，军队仍然是美国最受高度尊崇的公共机构。

sentences.en: And I think there are a lot of good reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这背后有很多充分的理由。

sentences.en: But it has also sort of led to a sense that we're supermen, that the military can accomplish almost the impossible.
sentences.zh: 但这也在某种程度上导致了一种观念，即我们是超人，军队几乎可以完成任何不可能的任务。

sentences.en: And so we look at a situation like the Strait of Hormuz is closed and we think, we can open that.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们看到霍尔木兹海峡关闭这样的情况时，我们会想：我们能打开它。

sentences.en: Of course we can open that.
sentences.zh: 我们当然能打开它。

sentences.en: So just give us some perspective on, as a practical, realistic matter, why is it hard?
sentences.zh: 所以，请从实用和现实的角度给我们讲讲，为什么这很难？

sentences.en: Why would it be hard to force open the Strait of Hormuz or would it be hard?
sentences.zh: 强行打开霍尔木兹海峡为什么会很难？或者说它本来就很难？

sentences.en: Yeah, it would be hard to keep it open.
sentences.zh: 对，要保持它的畅通会很难。

sentences.en: And so it is like what we found in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 这就像我们在伊拉克所发现的那样。

sentences.en: We could bomb Iraq pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 我们轻而易举就能轰炸伊拉克。

sentences.en: We could even take Baghdad with relative ease.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可以相对轻松地攻占巴格达。

sentences.en: We could get rid of the existing government.
sentences.zh: 我们可以除掉现有的政府。

sentences.en: But once we wanted to change the reality on the ground, who actually controlled things, how things worked.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们想要改变地面的现实，改变谁在实际控制、事情如何运转这些问题时。

sentences.en: Now you're not at 30,000 feet.
sentences.zh: 你就不再是站在三万英尺的高空了。

sentences.en: You're at six feet.
sentences.zh: 你是在六英尺的高度。

sentences.en: And you're the same height as your potential opponent.
sentences.zh: 你和你的潜在对手站在同一高度。

sentences.en: And I tell people about this war.
sentences.zh: 我对人们谈起这场战争时总是这样说。

sentences.en: If you like this war, enjoy this first part, because this is the best part.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这场战争，那就好好享受前半段吧，因为这是最好的一部分。

sentences.en: Because everything after this will be harder, because it will be more equal.
sentences.zh: 因为这之后的一切都会更艰难，因为双方将更加势均力敌。

sentences.en: Even though we will have bombed them, we'll have to get down to a level, like in the Strait of Hormuz,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们轰炸过他们，但我们还是得回到某个层级，就像在霍尔木兹海峡一样，

sentences.en: where we've got ships potentially facing mines or even autonomous surface and undersurface aircraft.
sentences.zh: 我们的舰船可能会面临水雷，甚至水面和水下无人载具的威胁。

sentences.en: All the different threats that they can bring out just to make it lousy.
sentences.zh: 他们可以使出各种各样的威胁，只为了让情况变得一团糟。

sentences.en: And they're not all coming after U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且他们并不是全都冲着美国的

sentences.en: warships.
sentences.zh: 军舰去的。

sentences.en: They don't have to.
sentences.zh: 他们没必要那样做。

sentences.en: They only have to shoot a civilian tanker or a cargo vessel, you know, once a week.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要每星期袭击一艘民用油轮或货船，你知道的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then people go, well, I don't know what day they're going to strike somebody, so I'm not going to let my ships go now.
sentences.zh: 然后人们就会说，好吧，我不知道他们哪天会袭击谁，所以我现在不能让我的船出海了。

sentences.en: And so they can have an effect with a fairly low level of effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们只需付出相当低的作战成本，就能产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And the insurers won't insure the ships in that circumstance.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，保险公司不会再为这些船只承保。

sentences.en: The financial risk becomes unacceptable, which renders it virtually impossible to transit the Strait.
sentences.zh: 财务风险变得不可接受，这就使得通过该海峡变得几乎不可能。

sentences.en: Because nobody's doing that with no insurance, with total financial exposure.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人会顶着完全的财务风险、在没有保险的情况下做这种事。

sentences.en: So, General, when we're talking about the risks of the current war, there's been such an emphasis on the economic risk.
sentences.zh: 那么，将军，当我们谈到当前战争的风险时，各界对经济风险给予了极大的强调。

sentences.en: In other words, that if the Strait of Hormones remain closed or nearly closed, that we're going to talk about higher gas prices, rippling economic problems across the globe.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果霍尔木兹海峡保持关闭或接近关闭状态，我们将面临更高的油价，并在全球范围内引发一连串的经济问题。

sentences.en: We've been hearing about budgetary risks.
sentences.zh: 我们一直听到关于预算风险的讨论。

sentences.en: The administration is seeking $200 billion or more.
sentences.zh: 政府正在寻求2000亿美元甚至更多的资金。

sentences.en: But there's also another risk, which is above these, the risk to the human lives of the soldiers, sailors, airmen, Marines who are out there.
sentences.zh: 但同时还有另一种超越这些的风险，即身处前线的士兵、水兵、空军和海军陆战队员的生命安全风险。

sentences.en: And so how are you seeing the risk here to human life?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何看待这里对人类生命的威胁的？

sentences.en: What kind of escalating risks would we be facing to our own service members in this conflict?
sentences.zh: 在这场冲突中，我们自己的现役军人将面临怎样不断升级的风险？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's great to bring up because we've fortunately suffered few casualties to date.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得提出这一点非常好，因为幸运的是，到目前为止我们的伤亡很少。

sentences.en: But every casualty has a family and carries a loss, and we need to remember that.
sentences.zh: 但每一个伤亡背后都有一个家庭，都承载着一份悲痛，我们必须铭记这一点。

sentences.en: But if the war were to drag on, and for example, if it gets grittier, if we get forces on the ground, whether they're inside Iran or in neighboring areas, casualties will go up.
sentences.zh: 但如果战争久拖不决，例如，如果战局变得更加残酷，如果我们把地面部队派进去——无论是在伊朗境内还是在周边地区，伤亡人数就会上升。

sentences.en: Frustration will go up.
sentences.zh: 挫败感也会上升。

sentences.en: Now, we have a volunteer military now, so it's largely limited to people who self-selected in.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们实行的是志愿兵役制，所以参军的基本上只限于那些自愿报名的人。

sentences.en: But the reality is there is part of our society that goes in the military, and there's a lot of our society that does not.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我们社会中只有一部分人参军，而很大一部分人并没有。

sentences.en: And there starts to be a divide that comes from that and a resentment.
sentences.zh: 由此便开始产生一道分水岭和一种怨恨情绪。

sentences.en: And those are dynamics that you don't see early in a war, but over time come home.
sentences.zh: 这些都是你在战争初期看不到、但随着时间推移会逐渐显现的动态。

sentences.en: So, General, one thing that concerns me is this sort of civilian-military divide, that we do have only a very small percentage of people who serve.
sentences.zh: 所以，将军，我关心的其中一件事就是这种军民脱节，即我们只有极小比例的人口在服役。

sentences.en: The greatest – I believe it's still the case that the greatest indicator of service for you is that you had a family member serve.
sentences.zh: 最大的——我相信现在依然如此——你是否参军的最大指标，就是你的家族成员是否服过役。

sentences.en: So it's a small, self-perpetuating part of our culture.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们文化中一小部分自我延续的群体。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure that's necessarily healthy for us over the long term that we essentially have a soldier caste or a warrior class that defends this democracy,
sentences.zh: 我不确定从长远来看，这对于我们来说是否健康。我们实质上拥有一支防卫这个民主国家、

sentences.en: but is increasingly separate from the rest of our society and culture.
sentences.zh: 但却与社会的其余部分和主流文化日益隔绝的士兵阶层或武士阶层。

sentences.en: One of the questions I have is do you see that yourself also, and do you think that that could result potentially in a too great a willingness to use force?
sentences.zh: 我的问题之一是，你自己是否也看到了这种现象？你认为这是否有可能导致过于轻易地诉诸武力？

sentences.en: Obviously, we have an extremely respected military, very trusted military, but do you see warning signs in that kind of divide?
sentences.zh: 显然，我们拥有一支极其受人尊重、极受信任的军队，但你在这种脱节中看到了什么警示信号吗？

sentences.en: Well, I do on several ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在几个方面确实看到了。

sentences.en: One, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 第一，我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: It's not healthy to have a military caste grow up, even though it's been largely professional and apolitical and all the good things.
sentences.zh: 滋生出一个军事阶层是不健康的，哪怕它在很大程度上是专业的、非政治化的以及所有这些美好的品质。

sentences.en: But if you think about it, the propensity to go to war, at the end of the day, people who are professional soldiers, they have a reason to want conflict.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细想想，挑起战争的倾向——归根结底，职业军人是有渴望冲突的理由的。

sentences.en: I mean, the reality is it gives you a chance to work your craft and promotions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现实情况是，冲突能给你提供实践专业技能和晋升的机会。

sentences.en: I mean, so they wouldn't even really think about it directly, but you become incentivized for the kinds of military actions that give that opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，虽然他们可能不会直接去这么想，但你确实会被激励去支持那些能提供这种机会的军事行动。

sentences.en: Plus, it increases defense budgets and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 此外，这还会增加国防预算等等。

sentences.en: And then the other great danger is the more insulated the force is, the more potential for politicization,
sentences.zh: 另一个巨大的危险是，军队越是封闭孤立，政治化的可能性就越大，

sentences.en: particularly you have in the current environment where there have been generals fired simply because they don't fit in politically to the current administration.
sentences.zh: 特别是当你处在当前的环境下——有些将军仅仅因为在政治上不合现政府的胃口就被解雇了。

sentences.en: You start to shape that military and it starts to maybe align with a certain political leaning.
sentences.zh: 当你开始这样塑造军队时，它就会开始在某种程度上与特定的政治倾向靠拢。

sentences.en: When I was in the service, you never knew what your peers felt politically.
sentences.zh: 我在服役的时候，你绝不知道你的同僚在政治上有何感受。

sentences.en: You never talked about it.
sentences.zh: 你们从不谈论这个。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that that's under pressure.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种传统正面临压力。

sentences.en: And so I think the danger of having this separate entity is that after a while, it starts to think of itself as, as we've seen in some countries,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为拥有这样一个独立实体的危险在于，过了一段时间后，它会开始像我们在某些国家看到的那样，

sentences.en: sort of the guardians of the republic or of the nation.
sentences.zh: 把自己视为共和国或国家的守护者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So let's even get a little bit bigger picture for a moment.
sentences.zh: 那我们把视野放得更宏观一点。

sentences.en: How do you see this conflict fitting in with a more global grand American strategy?
sentences.zh: 你认为这场冲突如何契合更广泛的全球宏观美国战略？

sentences.en: Or does it fit in with a particular grand American strategy?
sentences.zh: 或者说它是否契合某种特定的宏观美国战略？

sentences.en: Because we've had a lot of debates over the 10 years of the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 因为在特朗普时代的这十年里，我们进行过很多辩论。

sentences.en: Is he isolationist?
sentences.zh: 他是奉行孤立主义吗？

sentences.en: And I think that that has sort of people have turned the page on that.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对这一点已经翻篇了。

sentences.en: Is he a guy who is interested in spheres of influence?
sentences.zh: 他是一个对势力范围感兴趣的人吗？

sentences.en: Where are you seeing the Trump sort of, for lack of a better term, grand strategy in Trump 2.0?
sentences.zh: 在特朗普2.0时代，依你之见，特朗普的宏观战略——如果换个更好的词的话——究竟是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think the first thing we saw that was obvious is the America first idea economically.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们首先看到显而易见的一点，就是在经济上奉行“美国优先”理念。

sentences.en: The tariffs were designed to encourage on-shoring, things like that.
sentences.zh: 关税旨在鼓励制造业回流，诸如此类。

sentences.en: The direct confrontation economically with China, same thing.
sentences.zh: 在经济上与中国直接对抗也是如此。

sentences.en: But then you step back from that and you say, okay, what really provides security in a world that's interconnected?
sentences.zh: 但如果你退一步来看，然后会问，好吧，在一个高度互联的世界里，究竟是什么在真正提供安全？

sentences.en: We can onshore things, but the reality, it's still interconnected and it's going to stay that way.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把制造业搬回国内，但现实是，它依然是互联的，而且将保持这种状态。

sentences.en: We're not going to undo that.
sentences.zh: 我们无法逆转这一点。

sentences.en: Well, in my view, it is credibility in the world.
sentences.zh: 依我看，这就是在世界上的信誉。

sentences.en: It is alliances.
sentences.zh: 这就是同盟关系。

sentences.en: It is relationships you can trust on.
sentences.zh: 这就是你可以信任的伙伴关系。

sentences.en: It is the rule of law writ large, international norms and rules and things like that.
sentences.zh: 广义上讲，这就是法治、国际规范和规则之类的东西。

sentences.en: And I think President Trump took most of those on and said, they're unfair to America.
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普总统对其中大部分都提出了质疑，并认为它们对美国不公平。

sentences.en: You allies don't carry your weight or any number of things.
sentences.zh: 你们这些盟友没有尽到自己的责任，诸如此类的事情还有很多。

sentences.en: And so, he weakened institutions.
sentences.zh: 因此，他削弱了各项制度。

sentences.en: He challenged norMs.
sentences.zh: 他挑战了既定规范。

sentences.en: He, in many cases, eliminated relationships that we had under the idea that that was going to advantage the strongest dog left on the block, which would be us.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，他打破了我们原有的关系，其核心理念是这能让场上剩下的那头最强大的恶犬占到便宜，也就是我们自己。

sentences.en: And I think that's proven not to be true.
sentences.zh: 而我认为事实证明并非如此。

sentences.en: You can't be that strong to do that.
sentences.zh: 你不可能强大到能为所欲为。

sentences.en: I think the recent adventurism, I'll call it, I think it comes from this idea that there was a fair amount of success in threatening people early.
sentences.zh: 我认为近来的这种冒险主义——我姑且这么称呼它——我觉得它源于这样一种观念，即早期通过威胁别人取得了相当大的成功。

sentences.en: I could threaten Canada.
sentences.zh: 我可以威胁加拿大。

sentences.en: I could threaten Greenland.
sentences.zh: 我可以威胁格陵兰岛。

sentences.en: And there was no cost to it.
sentences.zh: 而且这样做没有任何代价。

sentences.en: Now, there was no military action taken, but there was no cost to it.
sentences.zh: 当然，虽然没有采取军事行动，但确实没有任何代价。

sentences.en: And then shooting at the drug boats in the Caribbean was sort of a muscular way to do something.
sentences.zh: 然后，向加勒比海的毒品船开火，算是一种展现力量的举动。

sentences.en: I don't think it had any effect, but to do something.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它其实没什么实际效果，但总归是做了点事。

sentences.en: The Maduro raid, I think, crossed a point in which the president got seduced by one of the things I mentioned,
sentences.zh: 马杜罗突袭行动，我认为，突破了一个临界点，当时总统被我刚才提到的一种想法所诱惑，

sentences.en: the idea that you can do something on the cheap if you're clever enough and you can pull it off.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果你够聪明并且能成功脱身，你就能以极低的成本办成事。

sentences.en: The thing about special operations missions is they are high risk.
sentences.zh: 特种作战任务的特点在于它们具有极高的风险。

sentences.en: And we say, well, they're high risk, but they always work.
sentences.zh: 而我们总说，好吧，它们风险很高，但它们总是能成功。

sentences.en: No, they don't.
sentences.zh: 不，它们并不总是成功。

sentences.en: That's what makes them high risk.
sentences.zh: 这正是它们高风险的原因所在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think he got emboldened by that.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得他受到了这种成功的鼓舞。

sentences.en: And then I think that the other dynamic was, of course, Israel.
sentences.zh: 接着我认为另一个动态因素自然就是以色列。

sentences.en: The October 7th attacks created a dynamic in Israel and then the operations in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 十月七日的袭击在以色列引发了连锁反应，随后便是在加沙的军事行动。

sentences.en: And then there has been a dynamic driven by Prime Minister Netanyahu largely to expand Israel's security, expand Israel's power,
sentences.zh: 再后来，在很大程度上由内塔尼亚胡总理主导了一系列动态，旨在扩大以色列的安全、扩大以色列的权力，

sentences.en: expand all of the things that he would like and to do away with the boogeyman, which was Iran.
sentences.zh: 扩大所有他希望得到的东西，并彻底消灭那个被称为伊朗的恶魔。

sentences.en: Those became just absolutely defining objectives that President Trump had always been in sympathy with.
sentences.zh: 这些成为了绝对核心的目标，而特朗普总统对此一直都是赞同的。

sentences.en: And now I think he sort of got caught up in the current of, you know, it starts moving that way.
sentences.zh: 现在我觉得他有点被卷入那种势头中了，你知道的，事情开始朝那个方向发展。

sentences.en: Well, you know, there was a phrase used before October 7th, mowing the lawn or mowing the grass,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道的，在十月七日之前有一个常用的词，叫做“割草”或“修剪草坪”，

sentences.en: where essentially periodically you have conflict with Hamas or Hezbollah and you knock them back.
sentences.zh: 也就是基本上定期与哈马斯或真主党发生冲突，然后把他们打退。

sentences.en: You knock them back on their heels and it takes them months or years to recover and you just can sort of cycle, rinse, repeat and just keep doing that.
sentences.zh: 你把他们打得节节败退，他们需要几个月甚至几年才能恢复，然后你就可以循环往复、不断重复这个过程。

sentences.en: But I think October 7th, in my view, should have blown up that idea that that they had, quote unquote, mowed the grass time and time again.
sentences.zh: 但我认为十月七日这一天，依我之见，彻底粉碎了他们那种所谓一次又一次“修剪草坪”的想法。

sentences.en: And then Hamas, far from being cowed, was plotting this horrific, horrific, purely evil massacre.
sentences.zh: 而且哈马斯不仅没有被吓倒，反而一直在策划这场可怕至极、纯粹出于邪恶的大屠杀。

sentences.en: And so that creates a situation.
sentences.zh: 因此这就造成了一种局面。

sentences.en: You have threatening enemies.
sentences.zh: 你面临着充满威胁的敌人。

sentences.en: You have enemies who wish you harm, but you have no real capacity.
sentences.zh: 你面临着对你怀有恶意的敌人，但你却没有真正的能力。

sentences.en: You have an enormous capacity to damage them, but you have no real capacity to eliminate them, to destroy them.
sentences.zh: 你有能力对他们造成巨大的破坏，但你却没有真正彻底消灭他们、摧毁他们的能力。

sentences.en: It's a serious strategic dilemma.
sentences.zh: 这是一个严重的战略困境。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And we've seen it around the world.
sentences.zh: 我们在世界各地都看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You see it in the West Bank now.
sentences.zh: 你现在就能在约旦河西岸看到。

sentences.en: You see the reality that all of the resentment you create through what you do now, at some point comes back to you.
sentences.zh: 你会发现这样一个现实：你现在通过自己的所作所为制造的所有怨恨，在某个时刻终究会反噬到你身上。

sentences.en: I think that for everyone we kill in bombing Iran, they have a brother, sister, father, mother, and they are unlikely to go, oh yeah, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们在轰炸伊朗时每杀死一个人，他们就有一个兄弟、姐妹、父亲、母亲，他们不太可能会觉得：“哦，没关系。”

sentences.en: You killed my father, but yeah, it was geopolitical necessity on your part.
sentences.zh: “你杀了我父亲，但好吧，这从你们的角度来看是地缘政治的必需。”

sentences.en: But no wars that I'm familiar with are neat, clean, or produce the kind of outcome we actually want.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，没有任何一场战争是干净利落的，或者能产生我们真正想要的结果。

sentences.en: They produce this messy thing that might be better than before the war, but it's not a lot better.
sentences.zh: 战争产生的是一地鸡毛的乱局，或许比战前要好一点，但也并没有好到哪里去。

sentences.en: So let's move on to some other issues.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈其他一些问题。

sentences.en: So one of the things that I am often asked about is leadership and leadership within the military.
sentences.zh: 人们经常问我的一类问题关于领导力，以及军队内部的领导力。

sentences.en: And, you know, you have been described as one of the finest leaders of men in combat in the modern American military.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你曾被描述为现代美军中在战斗中最优秀的军人领袖之一。

sentences.en: And what we are seeing right now in the current secretary of defense is a very, an enormous amount of bravado of, you know, sort of a, we are lethal.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在从现任国防部长身上看到的，是一种非常、极其强烈的虚张声势，也就是某种“我们是致命的”，

sentences.en: We, we will kill you.
sentences.zh: “我们，我们会杀了你。”

sentences.en: We will destroy you.
sentences.zh: “我们会消灭你。”

sentences.en: You've got the, you've got the, you know, the bench pressing and the pushups and the, all of the, everything.
sentences.zh: 你看到的是，你看到的是卧推、俯卧撑以及所有这些、方方面面。

sentences.en: And I get a lot of questions, how does this land with soldiers?
sentences.zh: 我经常听到这样的疑问：士兵们对这套作风怎么看？

sentences.en: And my perspective, it has been, well, with some soldiers at land, they really like it.
sentences.zh: 而我的看法一直是，有些士兵其实挺喜欢这一套的。

sentences.en: You know, they like it when a senior leader will get their hands dirty.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当高级将领愿意亲力亲为时，他们会很欣赏。

sentences.en: They like it when a senior leader is fit and that they can share, like they can do the same things that the, the guys on the line do.
sentences.zh: 当高级将领体能出色，并且能够与前线士兵同甘共苦、做一样的事情时，他们会很喜欢。

sentences.en: But at the same time, in my experience, bravado is not necessarily really appreciated.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，根据我的经验，虚张声势并不一定真的受人认可。

sentences.en: It's a more of a show, don't tell culture in the military.
sentences.zh: 军队里更崇尚的是“用行动说话，而非夸夸其谈”的文化。

sentences.en: You've led men in combat for much of your life.
sentences.zh: 你的大半生都在战场上率领部下。

sentences.en: Talk to me a bit about sort of that line between sort of bravado and cool, calm professionalism.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊虚张声势与冷静沉着的专业精神之间的那条界线吧。

sentences.en: How do you see all of that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这一切的？

sentences.en: Um, I'm disappointed by the current atmosphere that is communicated from the top.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于从高层传达出的这种现行氛围，我感到很失望。

sentences.en: I had the honor and opportunity to serve with some of the most elite forces, people who really did some extraordinary things, but they didn't beat their chest about it.
sentences.zh: 我有幸与一些最精锐的部队并肩作战，他们做过一些真正非凡的事情，但他们从不为此拍胸脯自吹自擂。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And they weren't braggadocious and they didn't talk about, yeah, we love killing people.
sentences.zh: 他们不自大，也不会到处说“耶，我们喜欢杀人”。

sentences.en: That's just not the way they behaved.
sentences.zh: 他们的行事风格根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: Now, the danger though, of some of that verbiage now is much of the force is 18 years old and, and it's influenceable and they see that and they go, wow,
sentences.zh: 然而，现在这种言论带来的危险在于，部队里很大一部分人只有18岁，而且容易受影响，他们看到这些就会想，哇，

sentences.en: that's the way we ought to think.
sentences.zh: 这才是我们该有的思维方式。

sentences.en: That's the way we ought to be.
sentences.zh: 这才是我们该有的样子。

sentences.en: We are superior.
sentences.zh: 我们高人一等。

sentences.en: And there's another reality that even in, particularly in today's military, you know, the number of people who really need to have big biceps and be able to kick open the door is,
sentences.zh: 还有一个现实是，即使在、尤其是今天的军队中，那些真正需要拥有巨大二头肌并能够一脚踹开大门的人数，

sentences.en: is minuscule.
sentences.zh: 是微乎其微的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Because most of the force is intelligence, communications, logistics, all the enablers that allow you to, with great accuracy, put that very small number of operators.
sentences.zh: 因为军队的大多数人员从事的是情报、通信、后勤以及所有那些能够让你以极高精准度部署那一小部分特战人员的后方保障工作。

sentences.en: So when you say all people should look like me, that would be a disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以当你口口声声说所有人长相都应该像我一样时，那将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: You know, I think people ought to look like whatever they look like so that they are capable in their jobs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为大家长成什么样都无所谓，只要他们能够胜任各自的工作就行。

sentences.en: I think, you know, the idea that we wouldn't want gay or transgender service members to serve if they're good is preposterous.
sentences.zh: 我认为，那种认为如果同性恋或跨性别军人表现优秀却不准他们服役的想法简直荒谬绝伦。

sentences.en: I want who's ever good to serve.
sentences.zh: 只要表现优秀，我都欢迎他们来服役。

sentences.en: And you also get different perspectives.
sentences.zh: 而且你还能获得不同的视角。

sentences.en: And what we found in the counter-terrorist force, when I was young, it was sort of homogenous.
sentences.zh: 我们在反恐部队中发现，在我年轻的时候，人员结构某种程度上比较单一。

sentences.en: It was sort of white males with, you know, good posture.
sentences.zh: 基本上都是白人男性，而且，你知道的，体态挺拔。

sentences.en: And by the time you got to Iraq 2007, as we had matured, it had become a meritocracy of older men and women, young people,
sentences.zh: 而到了2007年的伊拉克，随着我们的成熟，它已经变成了一个由年长官兵、年轻人组成的精英管理体制，

sentences.en: all this different because they had proven they were contributory to the fight.
sentences.zh: 所有人多元融合，因为他们已经证明了自己对战斗的贡献。

sentences.en: So your ticket to being accepted was no longer just your bench press.
sentences.zh: 因此，你被接纳的通行证不再仅仅是你的卧推成绩。

sentences.en: It was now, are you smart?
sentences.zh: 现在看的是，你聪明吗？

sentences.en: Are you committed?
sentences.zh: 你有奉献精神吗？

sentences.en: Will you be a good colleague?
sentences.zh: 你会是个好队友吗？

sentences.en: And that became a much healthier force.
sentences.zh: 这让军队变成了一个健康得多的肌体。

sentences.en: If we would think that way, I think it's a healthier way for military service to be.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能秉持这种思维方式，我认为这才是军旅服务应有的更健康的形态。

sentences.en: And I've had a problem with the word warrior.
sentences.zh: 而且我对“勇士”这个词一直有点意见。

sentences.en: And it's not because you can't say, well, the warrior ethos is bad.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为你不能说“勇士精神是坏事”。

sentences.en: But traditionally, warriors were separate from soldiers.
sentences.zh: 但传统上，勇士和士兵是不同的概念。

sentences.en: And the difference between an army and a mob is discipline and leadership and the uniform code of military justice.
sentences.zh: 军队与乌合之众的区别在于纪律、领导力以及《统一军事司法法典》。

sentences.en: It's why we operate in a certain controlled way.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们以某种受到控制的方式行动。

sentences.en: Because when you give young people the ability to carry weapons that can take life, you have to have a level of discipline, part of which is values and culture.
sentences.zh: 因为当你赋予年轻人携带能够夺走生命的武器的能力时，你必须具备一定水平的纪律，其中一部分是价值观和文化。

sentences.en: And part of it is just military prescribed discipline.
sentences.zh: 而另一部分仅仅是军队规定的纪律。

sentences.en: It's essential.
sentences.zh: 这是至关重要的。

sentences.en: You know, if I think of it like this, big brains are more important than big biceps.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果让我来比喻的话，大智慧比大二头肌更重要。

sentences.en: And if any military force in the world is teaching us that right now, it's Ukraine, which has used innovation, especially in drone warfare.
sentences.zh: 如果说现在世界上有哪支军队正在给我们上这一课，那就是乌克兰，他们在创新方面表现卓著，尤其是在无人机作战领域。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They're still surprising us.
sentences.zh: 他们依然在不断给我们带来惊喜。

sentences.en: It feels like, I don't know, you know, you may be less surprised than me, General.
sentences.zh: 感觉上，我不知道，你知道的，将军，你可能比我受到的惊吓少一些。

sentences.en: But Ukraine is consistently surprising me every six to nine months with its extraordinary resilience.
sentences.zh: 但乌克兰每隔六到九个月就会以其非凡的韧性持续不断地带给我惊奇。

sentences.en: And, you know, just to switch gears a tiny bit from Iran, it feels to me as if one of the outcomes,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，稍微把话题从伊朗转开一下，我感觉如果能达成某种结果——

sentences.en: if we are able to achieve a satisfactory resolution in the fight against Ukraine's fight against Russia, that at the end of the day,
sentences.zh: 如果我们能够在乌克兰反抗俄罗斯的斗争中取得令人满意的解决方案，那么到头来，

sentences.en: we'll have added to the Western alliance one of the most capable militaries and most potent militaries in the world at the end of this conflict.
sentences.zh: 在这场冲突结束时，我们将为西方联盟增添世界上最具战斗力、最强大的军队之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, there is no way to take away the value of on the ground experience and that experience of having to innovate.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，实地经验以及被迫创新的经验其价值是无法替代的。

sentences.en: Armies don't innovate well in peacetime.
sentences.zh: 军队在和平时期是不善于创新的。

sentences.en: Too many limitations.
sentences.zh: 有太多的限制。

sentences.en: In wartime, particularly to survive, Ukraine has been just a hotbed of constant innovation.
sentences.zh: 在战争时期，特别是为了生存，乌克兰一直是不断创新的温床。

sentences.en: And so if we're not going to school on that and if we're not trying to replicate that energy to innovate in our force, then we're missing a requirement.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们不向他们学习，如果我们不试图在我们自己的军队中复制那种创新的活力，那我们就错失了一项必要的要求。

sentences.en: Well, General, you've been very generous with your time, but I wanted to end because I want you to give you a chance to tell me how wrong I am about something.
sentences.zh: 好吧，将军，你百忙之中抽出时间接受采访，但我最后想留点时间，让你有机会指出我在某些方面错得有多离谱。

sentences.en: And that is, you've been an advocate for national service, a mandatory national service for young people.
sentences.zh: 那就是，你一直倡导国民服役制度，针对年轻人的强制性国民服役制度。

sentences.en: And I'm a huge believer in service.
sentences.zh: 而我非常坚信服役的价值。

sentences.en: One of my greatest regrets in my life is I didn't join the military until I was in my mid-30s.
sentences.zh: 我人生中最大的遗憾之一，就是直到三十多岁才参军。

sentences.en: I wish I had done it when I was much younger.
sentences.zh: 我真希望自己能在年轻得多的时候就去参军。

sentences.en: General, I can tell you a 36-year-old lawyer in officer basic is not the greatest sight in the world, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 将军，我可以告诉你，一个36岁的律师出现在军官基础训练班里可真算不上什么美景，我必须得承认。

sentences.en: But I made it through.
sentences.zh: 但我还是挺过来了。

sentences.en: So I'm a huge believer in service, whether it's joining the military, Teach for America, Peace Corps, you name it.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常相信服役的意义，无论是参军、加入“为美国而教”项目、和平队，还是别的什么。

sentences.en: But that sort of libertarian side of me is saying it's too much to make people do it.
sentences.zh: 但由于我身上那种自由意志主义倾向，我会觉得强迫人们去做这事未免要求过高。

sentences.en: We should urge them.
sentences.zh: 我们应该劝导他们。

sentences.en: We should not make them.
sentences.zh: 而不该强迫他们。

sentences.en: But my understanding is you're an advocate of sort of a mandatory national service, not a conscription into the military necessarily, but national service.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，你是强制性国民服役的倡导者，倒不见得是强制征兵入伍，而是国民服役。

sentences.en: Tell me your perspective on that.
sentences.zh: 跟我谈谈你对此的看法吧。

sentences.en: Why is my voluntary emphasis going to be ultimately wrong?
sentences.zh: 为什么我那种坚持自愿的强调最终会是错误的？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's funny because when I first thought about national service, I thought mandatory.
sentences.zh: 对，这挺有意思的，因为当我最初考虑国民服役时，我脑子里想的就是强制性的。

sentences.en: And then they talked me off the ledge and they said, no, it needs to be voluntary.
sentences.zh: 然后他们劝我打消这个念头，对我说，不，这必须是自愿的。

sentences.en: And so for a decade, I hewed to the line that it should be voluntary, but expected, culturally expected.
sentences.zh: 所以在长达十年的时间里，我都坚持应当采取自愿原则，但要在文化上形成一种预期。

sentences.en: I'm back to mandatory now.
sentences.zh: 现在我又回到了强制支持者的立场上。

sentences.en: And so I go back to why did 36-year-old David French go into the military and go to serve?
sentences.zh: 所以我想回到这个问题：36岁的大卫·弗伦奇为什么要参军并去服役？

sentences.en: Because he was not the same person that he was at 17 or 18.
sentences.zh: 因为他已经不再是17或18岁时的那个自己了。

sentences.en: If you had been as mature then, you'd have done service then.
sentences.zh: 如果你那时候有那么成熟，你当时就会去服役了。

sentences.en: Maybe Teach for America or something.
sentences.zh: 也许是加入“为美国而教”或者别的什么。

sentences.en: The point is, my life choices at 17 or 18 weren't the beSt.
sentences.zh: 重点是，我在17、18岁时做出的生活选择可不是最好的。

sentences.en: And they're on record as having been very problematic.
sentences.zh: 而且有据可查，那些选择问题很大。

sentences.en: But the point is, I think if we wait for everybody to arrive at the right answer, just way too many.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，我认为如果我们等待每个人都自己想通得出正确的答案，那人数未免也太多了。

sentences.en: And you are affected by your peers and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 而且你难免会受到同龄人等等因素的影响。

sentences.en: I think if we just said, the heck with it, it's mandatory.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们直接宣布：管他三七二十一，这就是强制的。

sentences.en: And give a range of different options.
sentences.zh: 并且提供各种不同的选项供人选择。

sentences.en: But what I think it would do is it would be a great leveler in American society.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这样做会产生一个效果，它将成为美国社会的一大均质器。

sentences.en: It would be something that every American had to do.
sentences.zh: 这将是每个美国人都必须完成的事情。

sentences.en: And they would, when they got together later in life, they might joke about stuff, but they'd start the conversation.
sentences.zh: 当他们日后在生活中聚在一起时，也许会拿这些事开玩笑，但他们会以此开启对话。

sentences.en: Well, where did you serve?
sentences.zh: “哦，你当年在哪儿服役的？”

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, I taught in New Orleans.
sentences.zh: “我在新奥尔良教过书。”

sentences.en: I did X or, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: “我做过某某工作，”诸如此类。

sentences.en: And it would be a way to bridge divides.
sentences.zh: 这将成为弥合分歧的一种途径。

sentences.en: And, you know, all of us could use a period in our lives when we're doing something that's inconvenient or maybe unpleasant or that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们所有人都需要经历这样一段时期：在生活中做一些有些不便、甚至可能不太愉快或者类似的事情。

sentences.en: We come out better for it.
sentences.zh: 我们经历过后会变得更好。

sentences.en: And I know that says, who am I at 71 to tell young people what they ought to be doing?
sentences.zh: 我知道有人会说，我都71岁了，哪来的资格去告诉年轻人他们该做什么？

sentences.en: Well, if I can't do it now, when can I do it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我现在不能这么做，什么时候才可以？

sentences.en: Well, General, this has been a real pleasure.
sentences.zh: 将军，这次谈话真是太愉快了。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you giving me the chance to pick your brain on some of the most thorny issues that, you know, we're dealing with right now as a nation and a culture.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您给我机会，就我们国家和文化目前正在处理的一些最棘手的问题向您请教。

sentences.en: Very much appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 真的很感激。

sentences.en: Well, you're kind to have me, David.
sentences.zh: 哪里，你能邀请我来是我的荣幸，大卫。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。
